Sensitive input field blocked. Text was not inserted.

Some apps expose background placeholder text to Accessibility, which contaminates final insertion. When enabled, in target apps the floating ball switches to Select-All + Paste with an invisible marker to avoid placeholder issues. The clipboard may be used temporarily (best-effort restore). Works for Telegram, Douyin, etc.
Enter package or prefix (e.g., org.telegram). A trailing * means prefix match (e.g., org.telegram.*).
Accessibility: copy result to clipboard only

Applies only to the packages below: in these apps, when using floating voice input, copy the result to the clipboard instead of inserting via Accessibility APIs. If a line contains all, it applies globally.
Enter exact package names (e.g., com.tencent.mm). To apply globally, add a single line with all.
Please enable Accessibility Service in system settings to support this feature
Use volume keys for voice recognition
Shizuku permission requested. Please grant it in Shizuku.
Connecting to Shizuku. Permission prompt will appear once connected.
Shizuku is unavailable and root is not detected
Failed to start keep-alive via Shizuku / root
Unable to start microphone foreground service. Open the app once, then try again.
Allow floating ball and volume-key recording to insert ASR results into the current input field. No data is collected or uploaded.
Move mode enabled. Tap the ball to exit.
Keeps the app running with a persistent notification.
Shows recording status while the floating ball uses the microphone.
The floating ball will not be displayed. Voice recognition can only be accessed through the keyboard.

Enables the floating ball for voice recognition. You can use voice input from anywhere, even when the keyboard is hidden. Requires display overlay permission. Accessibility is still required for volume-key recording, and for Accessibility insertion when the IME bridge is not active.
The floating ball remains visible even when the keyboard is hidden.
The floating ball is automatically hidden when the keyboard is hidden and shown when the keyboard appears. Keyboard state can be detected by Accessibility or by an active IME bridge.
Moving the floating ball requires long-pressing to enter move mode or using the menu.
You can drag the floating ball directly to reposition it.
Volume keys keep their normal system behavior and will not control recording.
When a keyboard is visible, the Accessibility Service listens for volume key clicks to start or stop voice recognition. Long-press volume keys are not used.
Volume key recording starts and stops silently, except for existing error prompts.
Shows a short toast when volume keys successfully start or stop recording.
If the keyboard disappears while volume-key recording is active, recording continues until you stop it manually.
If the keyboard disappears while volume-key recording is active, recording stops automatically.
Floating results use the existing Accessibility insertion path or clipboard fallback.

When a compatible LSPosed or LSPatch bridge is active in the current third-party keyboard, final recognition text is inserted through that keyboard\'s InputConnection, and keyboard panel visibility is reported by the keyboard itself. This is an advanced option and does not read existing input text.
The bridge may still insert final text, but long-press recording inside the third-party keyboard will not be available.

Allows a compatible bridge module in the current default keyboard to start recording with that keyboard\'s microphone permission and push PCM audio to BiBi Keyboard. It does not start floating-ball or main-app microphone recording as a fallback.
Uses standard Accessibility API to insert text. Works for most apps.

For target apps, uses Select-All + Paste method to avoid background placeholder text contamination. The clipboard may be temporarily used (best-effort restore). Useful for apps like Telegram and Douyin.
Recognition results are inserted directly into the input field via Accessibility API.
For target packages, recognition results are copied to clipboard only, without automatic insertion. Useful for apps where direct insertion doesn\'t work properly.
No foreground service is kept. The system may reclaim the app more aggressively in background.
Starts a foreground service with a persistent notification to strengthen background keep-alive.
Starts the foreground keep-alive service normally. Some systems may block background restarts.
Uses Shizuku (or root) to periodically start the foreground keep-alive service with shell privileges to improve reliability. Requires Shizuku authorization or root.
